stage1.impression: A clear ball with an etched meteorite slice on a black puck against a cream sweep; the lower half of the ball is a flat milky white that merges with the backdrop, so the glass loses its volume and edge. The slice reads as a flat printed graphic with a stepped beige ghost along its left and bottom edges, and the base is a near-black silhouette.

blocking_9: The ball's lower hemisphere must separate from the sweep: today it is 237.7 median, range 6.7 (450,1250 to 1150,1400) against a sweep of 238.5 to 240.5; it needs a dark refracted band or gradient, at least 25 levels below the sweep
The sweep must fall off: today it is one value, 238.5 at the top and 238.7 to 240.5 lower down (range 1.8), so it reads as a flat card behind the object
The ball's silhouette needs a defined dark rim on both sides: the right rim step is 21.6 levels with a 0 px transition, the left 34.4
The slice must read as etched metal: the kamacite bands peak at p95 182, a matte grey, with no directional sheen across the band families
The base must show form: its side has median 17.4 and 12.5 % crushed, with no edge highlight or gradient
The stepped, faceted beige ghost at the slice's left and lower edge (the pocket wall seen through the acrylic) must render as a smooth thin line, not a stair-step

changes.problem: The lower hemisphere refracts only the bright sweep behind and above the object, so it is the same value as the backdrop and the ball reads as a white disc, not a solid sphere.

evidence.measured: lum_median 237.7, lum_range 6.7; sweep beside the ball at (100,1150 to 250,1300) is 240.5, range 1.2

changes.expected: A soft dark band refracted into the lower third of the ball, inverted by the lens, its median about 160 to 200, giving the sphere a dark lower edge against the sweep.

changes.problem: The sweep is evenly lit top to bottom, so there is no depth behind the object and nothing for the clear upper ball to read against.

evidence.measured: lum_median 238.5, range 1.8; lower sweep (100,1150 to 250,1300) 240.5: no falloff

changes.expected: The upper sweep drops to about 215 to 228 while the area near the floor stays near 232, a gentle vignette that also darkens the ball's refracted image.

changes.problem: The flags are too far out to put a dark edge reflection on the ball's rim, so the right silhouette is a 22-level step and the glass looks thin.

evidence.measured: edge: largest step 21.6, width 0 px; left rim (250,1000 to 380,1100) step 34.4

changes.expected: A dark reflected rim band about 15 to 30 px wide on both sides of the ball, its darkest pixels below 90.

changes.problem: The base's side is a crushed black block with no gradient or top-edge highlight, so the anodised aluminium has no form.
changes.expected: The base side lifts to a 35 to 60 median with a soft horizontal gradient; crushed pixels below 3 %.

changes.problem: The kamacite bands reach only a matte mid-grey, so the slice reads as a printed pattern, not polished and etched iron.
changes.expected: The bright bands rise to p95 about 195 to 215 while the plessite stays below 75 at p5, widening the slice's tonal range to about 130 to 150 levels.

changes.problem: There is no crisp highlight on the ball's upper shoulder, so the acrylic looks dull rather than polished.

evidence.measured: lum_median 211.4, lum_p95 239.7: no specular peak above the sweep's own value

changes.expected: A defined strip highlight on the upper-left shoulder reaching 245 to 252 at p95, without clipping.

out_of_scope.request: Smooth the dry pocket's outline (the stepped, faceted beige ghost at the slice's left and lower edge, around x 500 to 560, y 980 to 1240)
out_of_scope.why: It reads as a tessellation or modelling artifact and is the most visible fault at magazine size, but the pocket's geometry is fixed. The mesh resolution or the pocket's offset surface needs checking by whoever owns the model.

out_of_scope.request: Give the etched pattern relief or anisotropic sheen per band family
out_of_scope.why: The slice's surface and what is inside the ball are fixed. Without per-band reflectance the Widmanstatten figure stays graphic under any light.
